Claim Statement: NPCI UDIR circular lists 'Cash Withdrawal — Cash not received' and automates reversals, credit adjustments, and chargebacks via ReqChkTxn API between banks.
What the Source Proves: NPCI operates a backend interbank dispute engine (UDIR) for defined AePS failure workflows between member banks.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: UDIR is strictly an interbank B2B API switch protocol; it has no native customer-facing interface. Frontline BCs and users cannot directly view UDIR statuses.
Recommended Project Action: Position SaathiFlow as a frontline pre-grievance navigation co-pilot that complements backend UDIR without duplicating it.

Claim Statement: AePS monthly approved transaction volumes cited in original brief (462M–618M) and prior estimates (~80M–110M).
Source Title & Publishing Org: NPCI AePS Product Statistics Portal, NPCI
Evidence Classification: Disputed Estimate Removed; Primary Data Segmented
What the Source Proves: NPCI tracks AePS Cash Withdrawal, Aadhaar Pay, and Fund Transfers separately on its product statistics portal. Total PMJDY accounts stand at 53.5+ crore.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: The brief's 462M-618M monthly range is an unsupported statistical anomaly. Third-party estimates are unverified. National failure rates and dispute volumes are not publicly disclosed.
Recommended Project Action: Removed all disputed monthly volume estimates from official statistics tables. Replaced with transparent statement: 'NPCI tracks AePS metrics on its portal; disaggregated failure rates are not publicly available'.

Claim Statement: For ATM / Micro-ATM (Sl. No. 1) and AePS (Sl. No. 5) cash-out failures where account is debited without cash, RBI mandates auto-reversal within T+5 calendar days and ₹100/day delay compensation payable suo-motu.
Source Title & Publishing Org: Harmonisation of Turn Around Time (TAT) RBI/2019-20/67 DPSS.CO.PD No.629/02.01.014/2019-20, RBI
What the Source Proves: Statutory outer limit for auto-reversal is T+5 days (where T is transaction calendar date) with automatic ₹100/day penalty for delays without requiring a formal customer claim.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: Applies specifically to cash-not-dispensed micro-ATM debits and unconfirmed AePS merchant debits. Does NOT apply to declines without debit (e.g. biometric mismatch ISO 55). Suo-motu credit frequently fails when network logs drop out.
Recommended Project Action: Frame the ₹100/day penalty as a statutory legal entitlement that SaathiFlow actively calculates and enforces via Day-6 escalation letters.

Claim Statement: Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2021 (Clause 10) allows customer escalation if the bank has rejected the complaint wholly or partly (immediate right!) OR if 30 days have elapsed without a reply.
Source Title & Publishing Org: Reserve Bank - Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021 & Annual Report 2024–25, RBI
What the Source Proves: Customers have a quasi-judicial escalation mechanism; the 30-day waiting period has an explicit exception if the bank rejects the complaint earlier.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: Aggregated 2.96 lakh complaints across RBI Ombudsman offices cover all retail banking products (cards, loans, UPI, net banking); AePS complaints are not disaggregated.
Recommended Project Action: Corrected all references to the 30-day rule to include the bank rejection exception. Clarified that 2.96L complaints is an aggregate, not AePS-specific.

Claim Statement: Grievance redress mechanisms in digital payment applications largely fail constrained users due to complex terminology, buried menus, and rigid symptom categorizations.
Source Title & Publishing Org: Do UPI In-App Grievance Redress Mechanisms Work for Constrained Users?, Dvara Research
Evidence Classification: Verified for Smartphone UPI; Supported Only by Indirect Evidence for AePS
What the Source Proves: Constrained users experience severe anxiety and drop-off when confronted with rigid error taxonomies and English-heavy self-service portals.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: Evaluated smartphone UPI apps (Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm); findings cannot be treated as direct empirical proof of BC micro-ATM behavior without field validation.
Recommended Project Action: Treat transferability from smartphone UPI to rural BC micro-ATMs as a primary research hypothesis (H1) to be validated during Phase 2 field trials.

Claim Statement: Dvara Research published an open-access UPI GRM Toolkit providing conversational intake patterns, progressive disclosure models, and visual tracking prototypes.
Source Title & Publishing Org: UPI Grievance Redress Mechanism Toolkit, Dvara Research
What the Source Proves: Guided triage and conversational complaint intake have already been conceptualized and open-sourced for digital payments.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: The toolkit is optimized strictly for smartphone in-app UPI experiences; it does not address rural BC micro-ATM kiosks, biometric errors, or offline physical slips.
Recommended Project Action: Position SaathiFlow as a dedicated guided triage and incident recording tool specialized for assisted-agent rural BC micro-ATMs.

Claim Statement: Dvara Research uses automated NLP on public social media (X/Twitter) and app store reviews to monitor UPI consumer grievances across major payment providers (PARSE).
Source Title & Publishing Org: Market Monitoring of UPI Customer Issues (PARSE Methodology), Dvara Research
Scope (Geo/Pop): National / English & Romanized Hindi Social Posts
What the Source Proves: Automated NLP grievance trend analysis exists for public web feedback on UPI.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: Completely blind to offline rural AePS users who do not post on X (Twitter) or Google Play Store. Proves SaathiFlow must not replicate generic social media NLP.
Recommended Project Action: Reject generic social-media scraping; maintain SaathiFlow's focus on kiosk-level pre-grievance decision support.

Claim Statement: Ministry of Home Affairs operates Helpline 1930 and CFCFRMS to place administrative debit liens on suspect recipient bank accounts during the golden hour. Restitution requires Section 457 CrPC / 503 BNSS court order.
Source Title & Publishing Org: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal SOP & CFCFRMS, I4C / MHA
Evidence Classification: Verified by Official Portal SOP & Statutory Law
What the Source Proves: A dedicated law-enforcement and banking interbank lien mechanism exists for rapid fraud reporting.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: Freezing is contingent on funds remaining unwithdrawn in the immediate beneficiary account. Administrative liens do not disburse money back to victims without judicial authorization.
Recommended Project Action: Explicitly warn users that 1930 places a temporary lien to prevent fund siphoning, but formal money return requires a Section 457 CrPC / Section 503 BNSS Magistrate order.

Claim Statement: Over 53.5 crore Jan Dhan (PMJDY) accounts have been opened with deposit balances exceeding ₹2.3 lakh crore; over 67% of accounts are in rural/semi-urban areas reliant on Business Correspondents (Bank Mitras).
Source Title & Publishing Org: PMJDY Progress Report & Scheme Overview, DFS / MoF
What the Source Proves: Demonstrates the enormous demographic scale of rural citizens reliant on micro-ATMs and BCs for cash withdrawal.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: Total PMJDY accounts cannot be used as a proxy for the number of failed AePS transactions or aggrieved users; it only demonstrates demographic scale.
Recommended Project Action: Clearly label PMJDY volume as demographic context and addressable market scale, NOT as a failure or dispute count.

Claim Statement: To curb AePS fraud involving cloned silicone fingerprints, NPCI and UIDAI mandated STQC-certified Level 1 (L1) biometric devices with hardware liveness detection and disabled face authentication for cash withdrawals.
Source Title & Publishing Org: UIDAI & NPCI Security Mandates on Registered Devices (L1), NPCI & UIDAI
What the Source Proves: Biometric spoofing has been officially acknowledged as a major operational fraud vector necessitating hardware-level liveness enforcement.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: Protects capture at point of sale, but does not provide post-fraud recovery assistance to victims whose funds were already compromised.
Recommended Project Action: Integrate L1 device troubleshooting and mAadhaar biometric locking into SaathiFlow's post-fraud guidance.

Claim Statement: Rural customers travel 15–25 km to branch to resolve failed transactions.
What the Source Proves: Average distances between rural villages and bank branches often range from 5 to 20 km.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: No published empirical study isolates travel distance specifically for AePS dispute resolution. Must not be stated as a verified fact.
Recommended Project Action: Relabeled as an unverified working hypothesis (H3) to be measured via 10 customer interviews in Phase 2.

Claim Statement: Rural customers spend ₹150–₹300 on transport and lost daily wages visiting branches.
What the Source Proves: Estimate based on rural shared-auto fares and MGNREGA daily wage benchmarks (~₹200-250/day).
Limitations & Audit Verdict: Not verified by a published survey; actual costs vary significantly by region. Must not be stated as an established fact.
Recommended Project Action: Relabeled as an estimated economic hypothesis to be measured directly in customer interview protocols.

Claim Statement: Repeated fingerprint retries after timeout cause duplicate debits.
Evidence Classification: Supported Only by Indirect Evidence / Working Hypothesis
What the Source Proves: NPCI circulars warn against immediate retries; consumer forums report instances of multi-debits during latency.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: No disaggregated national dataset measures the exact frequency of duplicate debits caused by user retries.
Recommended Project Action: Relabeled as an operational risk hypothesis (H2) to be audited via BC kiosk logs in Phase 2.

Claim Statement: Customers suspect Business Correspondents of theft when cash is not dispensed.
What the Source Proves: Practitioners document frontline verbal conflict and agent reputational damage when micro-ATMs time out.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: Not quantified by a statistical survey; level of conflict varies by agent relationship with community.
Recommended Project Action: Relabeled as a qualitative field observation / working hypothesis (H3) awaiting structured BC interviews.

Claim Statement: BCs lack adequate failure receipts or plain-language guidance on micro-ATMs.
What the Source Proves: Micro-ATM terminals display cryptic 2-digit ISO codes (ISO 68, 91); many handheld POS devices lack paper rolls.
Limitations & Audit Verdict: Receipt availability varies by BC hardware model and network aggregator (PayNearby, CSC, bank-issued).
Recommended Project Action: Relabeled as an operational gap hypothesis to be evaluated through terminal mystery shopping.
